title: The 70-30 Conversation Gap: Students Use AI, Teachers Haven't Had the Talk
content:
Hi [Name],

A number surfaced across education communities this week that many principals will recognise immediately.

Seventy percent of teenagers use AI for schoolwork. Only thirty percent say a teacher has ever talked with them about using it safely. Just twenty-six percent have discussed how to evaluate whether AI-generated information is accurate.

This is not a cheating scandal hiding in the data. Students acknowledge the trade-off — many say AI leads them to fewer original ideas and that they feel they are missing real learning when they use it to complete assignments. They are using the tool without the conversation.

Globally, AI literacy mandates are landing faster than implementation plans. Teacher forums describe directives arriving days before term with no training, no curriculum integration, and no clarity on what appropriate use looks like in their subject. University faculty debate whether the goal is critical thinking or AI fluency — while students pass courses with summarizer tools and arrive unprepared for the next sequence.

In India, a parliamentary panel flagged the school-coaching split: classrooms teach one thing, entrance exams test another. CBSE is weaving JEE and NEET foundations into Class 9–10. Assam now requires counsellors in coaching centres and bans rank-based batch segregation. The reform theme is the same — close the gap between what students experience and what institutions are willing to discuss honestly.

Schools rebuilding credibility will publish a Conversation Gap Playbook: what gets discussed in week one, what proof is required on assignments, and how parents reinforce the same language at home.

EduHexa has supported 100+ institutions through parent-trust building, board-season communication, and admissions messaging — with partners seeing up to 129% admission increases when public voice matched classroom reality.

Reply YES and we will share it.
